parole.significato: a small round shield used for parrying; a buckler
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch bokelare, folk-etymological interpretation of French bouclier (“buckler”), linking it to Dutch beuk (“beech”). The French word came from Old French boucler, bucler, from Vulgar Latin *bucculārius (“bossed”), from Latin buccula (“boss”).
Borrowed from French foyer, from Middle French [Term?], from Old French foier, from Vulgar Latin *focārium, from Late Latin focārius, from Latin focus (“hearth”).
Borrowed from French fusain, from Vulgar Latin *fusago, from Latin fusus.
From troubleren, from French troubler (“to disturb”), from Old French trobler, trubler, from Vulgar Latin *turbulāre (with metathesis), from Latin turbāre.
